topic: Process of Preparing Farm-Brewed Jiwamrita Inoculant
questionText:
Arrange the traditional steps for preparing 200 liters of liquid Jiwamrita (enough for one acre of natural farming):
(I) Mix 10 kg of fresh Desi cow dung with 10 liters of Desi cow urine in a 200-liter plastic drum
(II) Add 2 kg of organic jaggery (or sugarcane juice) and 2 kg of pulse flour (besan) along with a handful of virgin forest soil
(III) Fill the barrel with 200 liters of chemical-free water and stir vigorously clockwise with a wooden stick
(IV) Keep the drum in shade covered with a moist gunny bag, stirring twice daily for 48 to 72 hours until microbial fermentation peaks

Choose the correct chronological/logical sequence from the options given below:

options.text: II -> I -> III -> IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: I -> II -> III -> IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT principle for Process of Preparing Farm-Brewed Jiwamrita Inoculant.

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: I -> III -> II -> IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Sustainable Agriculture in India (Process of Preparing Farm-Brewed Jiwamrita Inoculant):
I -> II -> III -> IV

Detailed Analysis:
Jiwamrita preparation: blend dung/urine, add jaggery/besan/virgin soil, dilute with 200L water, and ferment in shade for 2–3 days.
Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.

topic: Soil Organic Carbon (SOC) Crisis in Indian Agriculture
questionText: Decades of intensive chemical farming and burning of crop residues have caused Soil Organic Carbon (SOC) in many Indian soils to decline dangerously from 1.0% to below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Sustainable Agriculture in India (Soil Organic Carbon (SOC) Crisis in Indian Agriculture):
0.3 to 0.5%

Detailed Analysis:
Continuous synthetic fertilizer use without organic recycling has halved SOC across vast arable belts, impairing soil water retention and microbial biofertilizer efficacy.
Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.
